newsitem.title: INDIA: SQUASH-PROMISING BARADA UPSETS SEEDS TO REACH LAST EIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-PROMISING BARADA UPSETS SEEDS TO REACH LAST EIGHT.

text.p: Former world junior champion Ahmed Barada showed why he is widely tipped as a world senior champion of the future when he upset the seedings to reach the quarter-finals of the $105,000 Mahindra International on Wednesday.

The Egyptian conquered sixth-seeded Englishman Mark Chaloner in a thrilling contrast of styles in which the brilliantly-gifted Barada came from 11-12 down in the final game to win 15-14 7-15 9-15 15-11 15-12.

"I'm training a lot harder and last the long matches better now," said Barada, who produced a stream of fine volley-drops and wrong-footing kills but also played his part in the continual collisions and lets which blighted the contest.

Twice Barada was sent tumbling after colliding with his sturdy and consistent opponent. Once, when the third game was slipping away from him, the Egyptian lashed the ball angrily out of court and was given a code of conduct warning.
But he recovered his composure in the final two games and on the last crucial points produced inch-perfect drops from deep positions to win the match.

Defeat for Chaloner meant only two seeds progressed to the last eight. They are Australian title-favourite Rodney Eyles and defending champion Peter Nicol of Scotland, who beat former British champion Stephen Meads in straight games.
Nicol meets Barada in the quarter-finals.

England's Simon Parke continued his remarkable fightback from testicular cancer, which has forced him to spend the second half of 1996 rehabilitating from chemotherapy, by defeating Egyptian Amir Wagih in five games.
Parke now faces Zubair Jahan, who set aside traditional Pakistani notions of family seniority in beating his elder brother Zarak Jahan 15-8 15-8 15-12.
